title: Field probe synthesis + hypothesis notes — July 2026
body:
OVERVIEW:
This doc bundles raw notes from three week-long field probes (June 22–July 6), plus support-ticket scrape, and five follow-up 30m interviews with heavy API users. Goal: surface concrete feature asks, group them by likely impact/cost, and propose testable hypotheses to validate product moves.

METHOD & SAMPLE: 
- Sources: 18 support threads (priority: billing/latency/consistency), 5 interviews (engineering leads at AI-native startups), product analytics (top 10 endpoints by qps), and two dedicated customer success calls with enterprise pilot accounts.
- Rough persona split: small AI startups (4 interviews), mid-market product teams (6 support threads), one platform team at finance customer (enterprise).
- Note style intentionally rough — includes verbatim customer quotes and 'notes to self' TODOs.

KEY THEMES (synthesis):
1) Model consistency regressions are the highest pain when rolling new model versions. Users see subtle output drift and lack fine-grained traffic split controls (canary behavior isn’t enough).
2) Token-level cost visibility is useful but not actionable without per-route attribution and example-level traces.
3) Latency spikes on long contexts (>= 2k tokens) push customers to use smaller models; they want predictable tail latencies under mixed workloads.
4) Embeddings drift and index re-ingestion cost: customers need recommendations for when to re-embed vs incremental patching.
5) Private deployment networking and KMS UX is painful — onboarding docs too prescriptive, missing quickstart for common infra patterns (EKS + corporate KMS).
6) Error handling: many customers want structured error types (rate_limit, degraded_fallback, model_mismatch) surfaced in SDKs.

REPRESENTATIVE QUOTES (verbatim, abbreviated):
- "We rolled v2.1 and our intent classification flipped on edge cases — no one could roll back a subset of traffic." — Mid-market PM
- "Your billing table is great, but we can't reconcile cost to the routes generating tokens. We have to guess." — Startup eng lead
- "When the sequence grows, occasionally we see 2–5s spikes that break user-facing latency budgets." — Platform eng (finance)

PRIORITIZED FEATURE ASKS (ranked by perceived ROI):
A — High impact, medium dev cost
- Per-route token attribution and example trace: show actual requests (redacted) that drove tokens + a per-route cost estimate — acceptance: customer can point to top-3 cost drivers within console in <2 clicks.
- Canary-split with model-variant pinning: enable percent split by user-id hash + easy rollback per cohort — acceptance: CS pilot can run a 10% canary and rollback automatically when quality delta > threshold.

B — Medium impact, low dev cost (quick wins)
- Structured SDK errors: return stable error codes and fallback hint in SDKs (py/ts).
- Onboarding checklist for Private (EKS + KMS): one-page quickstart + appendix of common failures.

C — Long-term, higher cost
- Predictive tail-latency profiling and recommended batching/quantization profile per model and token distribution.
- Embedding maintenance assistant: policy suggestions for reembedding schedules (cron heuristics) + incremental patch API.

QUICK WINS (engineering-friendly list):
- Add per-request route id to billing export (CSV column) — small backend change + 1-week QA.
- Map SDK error enums in py + ts and ship with changelog note — 3-day dev + test.
- Consolidate Private onboarding note examples for KMS into two canonical templates (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) — docs-owner task.

HYPOTHESES FOR VALIDATION (measurable):
H1: If we expose per-route token attribution in Console, 60% of pilot customers will reduce query duplication (eg duplicate system prompts) within 30 days.
- Metric: reduction in tokens/active-user by route.
H2: Providing structured error enums reduces support ticket triage time by 40% for rate_limit/fallback cases.
- Metric: median time from ticket open -> triage resolved.
H3: A simple canary splitting UI reduces rollbacks (manual) by 30% in first 90 days for pilot customers.
- Metric: count of manual major-version rollbacks per account.

RISKS & OPEN QUESTIONS (notes to self):
- Privacy: showing request content in console for traceability is valuable, but redaction & PII policies must be ironclad. Need legal review.
- Billing export changes may break downstream customer parsers — add opt-in and versioned export.
- Can we implement model-variant pinning without major routing refactor? Might be a medium infra touch.
- Unknown: how many customers would use embedding assistant vs prefer manual ops? run a small survey.

NEXT STEPS & OWNERS (proposed):
- 07/16: CS -> run 3 quick follow-up micro-surveys to pilot accounts (owner: Marisol).
- 07/20: Eng PM sync to scope per-route token export (owner: Ethan Park).
- 07/23: Docs improvement PR for Private quickstart templates (owner: Zara Ahmed).
- 07/30: Set up 6-week pilot for per-route attribution with 3 willing customers (owner: Luis Ortega).

LINKS & ARTIFACTS:
- Raw interview notes (internal): link on Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/CS/field-probes/2026-07
- Related Jira: JIRA-RINF-1428 (billing: per-route export), JIRA-RINF-1434 (sdk: structured errors)
- Slack thread: #cs-field-probes — summarize outcome and ask for volunteers for pilot

MISC NOTES / BRAIN DUMPS:
- Could bundle small canary feature as 'rollout tags' rather than full percent splits to lower infra cost. Explore a heuristic: sample by hashed userId mod N and allow N to be configured per-route.
- Consider a 'cost-surge' alert tied to billing which suggests candidate routes to inspect (automated detective).
- TODO: prepare one-pager for legal on redaction thresholds for console traces.

END — quick read; feedback requested from eng-owners and product for prioritization matrix.
